newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's grain import needs seen modest - Goldthwait.
newsitem.headline: Russia's grain import needs seen modest - Goldthwait.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department General Sales Manager Chris Goldthwait said in Moscow on Friday that Russia's grain import needs would be fairly modest.

"We expect Russia's actual grain import needs to be relatively modest for historical standards," he said in a brief telephone interview. "We do expect that there will some grain imports...but I wouldn't expect a big change from last year."
Goldthwait said there were no signs that Moscow, once one of the world's largest grain buyers, would return to world markets with centralised government imports.
"I would not expect such a change," he said, adding that the government occasionally purchased a cargo, but did so through privatised firms.
He put Russian imports of U.S. grain over the past six months in the range of 200,000-400,000 tonnes, with much going to the Russian Far East.

"There is, I would say, a continual modest level of trade here," he said. "We see a lot of that trade is going through the Russian Far East and we're pleased with that business and want to encourage it."
But he said Russia was buying more grain from the former Soviet republics.
Kazakhstan and Ukraine are big suppliers to Russia, which has had two poor harvests in row and is off to a late start in spring sowing.
